'''''Scrophularia grandiflora''''' is a species of flowering plant in the figwort family ([[Scrophulariaceae]]) [[endemic]] to [[Portugal]].

==Description==
''Scrophularia grandiflora'' is a [[perennial]] [[rhizomatous]] pubescent herb with stems up to {{convert|1.80|m|ft|abbr=on}} tall, ramified at the base. [[Pinnation|pinnatisect]] leaves. [[Inflorescence]] is usually {{convert|24|-|110|cm|in|abbr=on}} long with a group of 10 flowers at the base and the rest around 2-6 flowers, opposed, occasionally alternate. [[Petal]]s are pinkish-flesh, upper lip is purple pink. [[Anther]]s are yellow, sometimes with bluish margins. [[Staminode]] is purple. [[Seed capsule]] is ovoid, very hard when mature and is brown or greenish brown. Seeds are brown-blackish.<ref name="iberica">{{cite web |title=Scrophularia grandiflora |url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/13_144_02_Scrophularia.pdf |publisher=[[Flora Iberica]] |access-date=23 January 2021}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Scrophularia grandiflora'' is [[endemic]] to central west [[Portugal]], mainly in the districts of [[Coimbra District|Coimbra]] and [[Leiria District|Leiria]], and partially on [[Santarém District|Santarém]] and [[Lisbon District|Lisbon]]<ref name="flora-on">{{cite web |title=Scrophularia grandiflora DC. |url=https://flora-on.pt/#/1Scrophularia+grandiflora |publisher=Flora-on |access-date=23 January 2021}}</ref> where it inhabits slopes and shoulders of paths, empty spaces and forest edges, preferably in shady, humid and somewhat disturbed places. Usually {{convert|400|-|500|m|ft|abbr=on}} altitude but is also found at much lower sites.<ref name="iberica" /><ref name="flora-on" /> Its habitat is focused largely on the area around [[Coimbra]].<ref name="flora-on" />
